tools.name: search_offers
tools.description: Search current startup credits and deals, including cloud credits, SaaS discounts, free tiers, grants, perks, and partner offers. Filter by query, vendor, or category and evaluate eligibility from typed company facts; unknowns remain explicit.

tools.name: compare_offers
tools.description: Compare two to ten startup credit or deal offers side by side, including value, access requirements, eligibility, freshness, and evidence. Unknown eligibility and unsupported stacking remain explicit.

tools.name: inspect_evidence
tools.description: Inspect the provenance behind startup credits and deals. Resolve one to ten exact revisions to supporting events and observations, including freshness and dispute status.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Track added, changed, withdrawn, and removed startup credits, discounts, free tiers, perks, and deals through Sourcey's signed change feed after an optional cursor.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_changes, search_readiness, get_readiness · Private data: search_readiness, prepare_declaration · Public sink: search_readiness, prepare_declaration · Destructive: search_readiness, get_readiness, prepare_declaration.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_changes, search_readiness, get_readiness · Private data: search_readiness, prepare_declaration · Public sink: search_readiness, prepare_declaration · Destructive: search_readiness, get_readiness, prepare_declaration

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_readiness" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
